candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

'And from thence I went towards the north to the ends of the earth, and there I saw a great and glorious device at the ends of the whole earth' — Enoch's northward journey reaches the cosmic north device. The 'great and glorious device' (Geez maxbar 'abiy wa-səbuh) Tewahedo cosmological tradition reads as the divine mechanism for weather: the storehouses of snow, rain, and wind from which the meteorological phenomena are dispatched per divine will. This pre-meteorological cosmology Tewahedo monasticism preserves as catechetical resource: weather is not merely natural but divinely-administered, and prayer for rain is real petition to the administering Most High.
